articles.title: Trumpiana: Name dropper, court basher, hoax buster!
articles.summary: US News: A new ‘High IQ’ superhero comes to the aid of embattled AIDonald Trump has taken another new title. Amid calls to slow down AI development and keep it.
articles.body: A new ‘High IQ’ superhero comes to the aid of embattled AIDonald Trump has taken another new title. Amid calls to slow down AI development and keep it under a tighter leash, the peacemaker turned warrior, part time builder and constant name changer donned another hat: The Hoax Buster!“I am the Hoax Buster,” declared the POTUS taking cudgels on behalf of his beloved AI that gives him his daily dose of adrenaline charged memes with a picture of a defiant looking Trump entering a New York court to face criminal charges.MAGA faithfuls echoed the sentiment with more memes with ‘WomenForTrump’ pinning a poster of him in combat uniform parodying the Ghostbusters movie franchise.“And I’m right now breaking another Hoax — That AI is going to take over, consume, and destroy the World, and that Robots will be marching into our Cities, and getting rid of us all!” he wrote.“This is even wilder than the RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA HOAX, or the Global Warming Scam,” said Trump proclaiming, “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!”“WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!” he said telling “Conspiracy Theorists, Treasonists, Traitors, and Leakers,” that AI would be “the Greatest Economic Development Engine in History — Bigger than Oil, Gold, Diamonds, or even the Internet.”Then as the now not so friendly Supreme Court handed Trump a major defeat by blocking sweeping restrictions on mail-in voting — used by about one-third U.S. voters in 2024 — for the midterm elections, Trump went ballistic.“The Supreme Court has really let our Country down! Certain Justices are petrified of these crazed and depraved Democrats, and are totally unable to show the courage necessary to save our America,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.Chiding the three justices he nominated for the bench – Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett – as not “the people I interviewed to serve” but “merely a shell of their original selves,” he hailed two conservative dissenting judges – Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito – as “legends.”“The Court’s inability and unwillingness to do the right thing for our Country will go down, in a very negative way, in the annals of History,” wrote Trump suggesting his criticism of the top court “will likely cost me dearly for years to come.”Meanwhile, as a Washington judge blocked another attempt to return Trump’s name to the iconic Kennedy Center for Performing Arts, he reportedly threw a “tantrum” forcing his handpicked board to vote for closing the building for a two-year renovation.Saying he deserved to have his name recognized for rescuing the institution, Trump threatened to block the $250 million overhaul if his name isn’t added to the institution.And as Trump was photographed looking at a printout of the center titled “Kennedy Center DEMOLIS…,” on Air Force One, a judge ordered the center’s board not to bring the building down without giving 30 days’ notice of construction plans.Thousands also gathered for a “Hands Around the Kennedy Center” protest against its closure organized by ‘Hands Off the Arts.’ Some wore costumes and booed when Trump’s name was mentioned.Meanwhile, in a continuing war over the United States Institute of Peace (USIP), an independent think tank created by the Congress, some of its board members went to court to prevent the administration from carving “Trump’s name into the façade of the iconic USIP headquarters building.”Trump’s name was affixed to the exterior of the building, using bolted-on lettering in December after the administration took it over by “blunt force, backed up by law enforcement officers from three separate local and federal agencies,” as a judge described it, during Elon Musk’s cost cutting DOGE days.That change already offended the USIP board members who filed the suit, but carving Trump’s name into the stone, they argued “would cause irreparable harm.”But an unfazed Trump kept crowing about the efforts made by him “‘in my spare time,’ to bring back the Beauty and Magnificence of the White House, to levels it has never seen before, not even after its construction in 1792.”“Like our Nation, under the Dumocrats, was in decline, the White House was a badly maintained ‘dump.’ Now, it is a Palace!” he boasted.And even as National Park Service officials acknowledged that Trump’s desired 250-foot triumphal arch in the nation’s capital will likely contribute “to adverse effects to historic properties,” they suggested the project must proceed nevertheless.“Such adverse effects cannot be fully avoided while retaining the location-dependent purpose of the undertaking,” the National Park Service wrote in its planning document cited by the Washington Post.Trump capped the week by “proudly” announcing a ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over what he called their “constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS.”Media outlets “shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States,” he wrote on Truth Social and claimed that the U.S. government paid “an illegal and ridiculous $8 Million Dollar subscription” to Politico.Telling reporters the new policy was the result of “cumulative stories over the last few years,” Trump said he will announce bans of “Other Fake News Media Outlets” soon in the latest escalation of his longtime media feud.Meanwhile, as ordered by Trump in July, the administration is moving forward with plans to put signs outside the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History warning visitors of what the White House calls ideological bias at the museum.Being prepared by the Interior department at a cost of about $7,000 each, the signs would probably thank a great historian named Trump for guiding them articles.title: Georgia cattle farmer’s 80-year-old family farm faces 225-acre land loss as Spalding County airport project moves toward construction
articles.summary: US News: A Georgia cattle farmer says his family’s farm is being dismantled as Spalding County moves ahead with plans for a new airport. Jeff Melin faces the l.
articles.body: A Georgia cattle farmer says his family’s farm is being dismantled as Spalding County moves ahead with plans for a new airport. Jeff Melin faces the loss of roughly 225 acres of his 450-acre property, which his family has owned for almost 80 years. The planned airport would occupy 730 acres and include a 6,000-foot runway and 124 hangars for express and corporate jets. In an interview with AgWeb, Melin described how the project is affecting his farm, including a 70-acre pecan grove containing trees more than a century old, several of which have already been cleared as work connected to the project begins. He said he has 90 days to empty a farm shop and expects to remove livestock from the operation. The airport project is scheduled to begin construction in 2026 and be completed in 2031.Spalding County airport to cover 730 acresThe proposed airport is across 730 acres in Spalding County and includes a 6,000-foot asphalt runway. At the edge of Melin’s 70-acre pecan grove, trees, many of them more than a century old, have already been cut down as construction-related work begins. Concrete poles have been installed as the pecan trees give way to power lines, with the runway planned to replace part of the existing grassland.The airport proposal dates back to 2012, when the existing Spalding County airport’s runway was considered too short and several potential locations were examined for a replacement. The proposed 730-acre site includes 124 hangars intended for express and corporate jets. The Georgia Department of Transportation has said the new airport would generate an estimated $24 million in economic impact each year for Spalding County.Farmer faces cattle and equipment losses from airport land acquisitionMelin said the land acquisition will affect not only the acreage itself but also the equipment, livestock and buildings that support his cattle operation. He told AgWeb that he has been given 90 days to clear a 40-by-60-foot shop containing decades of farm equipment. He said he does not yet have another building available and expects to have to remove at least 65 cows and 30 calves as a result.The farmer also questioned the valuation of the property being taken. He said the farm had been continually improved through spending on fertiliser, lime, weed control and other land-management work, but argued that these investments were not reflected in the valuation. Melin compared the offer with other nearby land sales, including a 100-acre cattle farm that he said sold for $75,000 an acre to Georgia Power. “Nope. They wouldn’t give me an honest dollar,” he told AgWeb.New Spalding County airport expected to be completed by 2031Reportedly, construction of the new Spalding County Airport is due to begin in 2026 and finish in 2031. The project follows years of studies covering environmental, archaeological and ecological issues, while Melin says he received letters and announcements rather than direct communication about the plans.For Melin, the dispute centres on what will happen to a family farm maintained for generations. He said his family had previously surrendered land for road widening when it was considered necessary for public safety, but sees the airport project differently. “Our farm was not for sale at any price because our lives were moulded around this land,” Melin told AgWeb. As construction moves forward, the proposed airport will transform part of the property from cattle pasture and a long-established pecan grove into infrastructure serving the new aviation facility.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Pakistani officials said Saturday that one of the suicide bombers who targeted a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa mosque was an Afghan national.The explosions killed at least 21 people—including 15 police officers offering Friday prayers at the mosque—and injured 103 others, with police personnel making up the majority of the casualties.According to an investigator, in addition to the attacker identified as an Afghan citizen, efforts to identify a second bomber are ongoing. articles.title: In 1975, a Michigan carpenter found an Edmund Fitzgerald life ring and lifeboat fragment washed ashore; five decades later, the pair sold for $150,000
articles.summary: US News: Discover the incredible story of how a life ring and lifeboat fragment from the SS Edmund Fitzgerald, found in 1975, sold for $150,000 at auction five decades later.
articles.body: Larry Orr was working as a carpenter along Michigan's Lake Superior shoreline in 1975 when he found a life ring from the SS Edmund Fitzgerald and a piece of wood from one of its lifeboats, two objects that were connected to one of the Great Lakes' most famous shipwrecks. The discovery came shortly after the 729-foot freighter disappeared in Lake Superior on November 10, 1975. The ship had been carrying iron ore from Superior, Wisconsin, toward Detroit when it encountered a powerful storm. According to the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History, the Fitzgerald faced winds reaching 75 mph, snow, and waves estimated at 25 feet. The vessel reported that it was taking heavy seas over the deck and had developed a bad list before disappearing from radar later that evening. The Coast Guard later located the wreck in about 530 feet of water, roughly 17 miles northwest of Whitefish Point. The ship had broken into two sections on the lake floor, and all 29 crew members were lost.However, the artifacts remained in his possession for decades rather than disappearing into the history of the sinking. The life ring was eventually loaned to the Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum at Whitefish Point, where visitors could see an object that was recovered from the aftermath of the disaster.The Fitzgerald became a permanent part of Great Lakes historyThe Edmund Fitzgerald had been one of the largest and best-known freighters operating on the Great Lakes, and its loss became the worst single accident in Lake Superior's history in terms of lives lost in one incident. The Great Lakes Shipwreck Historical Society records the sinking as November 10, 1975, with the wreck lying north-northwest of Whitefish Point. The ship disappeared suddenly and did not leave any distress call. The wreck's location and condition eventually provided more information, but did not produce a single explanation about what happened during the storm.For the families of the 29 crew members, however, the wreck remained a personal loss, and every November, memorial services continue to mark the sinking and remember those who died. The artifacts found by Orr therefore carried a significance that went beyond their physical connection to the ship, since they were pieces of material evidence from the shoreline aftermath of a disaster whose wreck still rests beneath Lake Superior.Five decades later, the objects returned to the auction blockOrr had agreed to transfer the life ring to the state as part of a settlement connected to a separate lawsuit, and after the arrangement attracted public attention, the state returned the artifact to him. Orr ultimately decided to sell the objects, and according to the Associated Press, the life ring and a piece of the lifeboat were offered together at a December 2025 auction by Detroit auction house DuMouchelles, about a month after the 50th anniversary of the Fitzgerald's sinking. The lot carried an estimate of $15,000 to $20,000 but received 32 bids before selling for $150,000.The auction listing identified the objects as a life ring from the S.S. Edmund Fitzgerald and a plank from Lifeboat 1, and the buyer was not publicly identified. For Orr, the objects had spent half a century as reminders of something he encountered on the Michigan shore in the immediate aftermath of the sinking. In 2025, they became one of the rare pieces of Edmund Fitzgerald history to reach a six-figure auction price.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'How is it possible?' Kejriwal and family get SIR notice in Delhi, EC responds
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and four members of his family have been served notices by .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and four members of his family have been served notices by the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office under the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Notices have been issued to Kejriwal, his wife Sunita Kejriwal, son Pulkit Kejriwal, and parents Gobind Ram Kejriwal and Gita Devi. Kejriwal is a registered voter in the New Delhi-40 assembly constituency.According to Delhi Election Commission documents, Arvind Kejriwal and five members of his family are among 110 voters from ‘Part-51, KG Marg’ in the New Delhi assembly constituency who have been issued notices.The party questioned the move saying, “Is everything happening in this country just to keep the Supreme Lord happy? @ECISVEEP, how is it possible that the names of three-time Delhi Chief Minister @ArvindKejriwal Ji and his family members are missing from the Delhi voter list?”EC responds to Kejriwal's SIR noticeThe Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), New Delhi, has said notices were issued to former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and his family members as their submitted Enumeration Forms did not contain sufficient details to establish their linkage with the electoral rolls of the last revision in their respective states.The ERO said, “the submitted Enumeration Forms were not complete in terms of details which would have enabled linkage of themselves with the electoral roll of the last revision of the respective states, which were not present in their submitted Enumeration Forms.”In a press statement, the ERO further said that notices were being issued in accordance with procedures established and communicated by the Election Commission to electors who could not be linked to the electoral roll of the last revision or whose linkage showed logical discrepancies.“ As per procedures established and communicated by ECI, Notices are being issued to the electors who could not be linked with the electoral roll of the last revision and those having logical discrepancies in their linking with the electoral roll of the last revision. Electors have to submit a reply/requisite documents to the ERO concerned on receipt of the Notice. Disposal of Notices will be completed by 29.10.2026,” the statement said.The Election Commission also said a notice was issued to Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta after her name appeared in the list of discrepancies during the ongoing SIR process.Following verification of her details and documents, her electoral entry was validated and will be included in the final electoral roll for AC-14 (Shalimar Bagh), scheduled to be published on November 4, 2026.The notices come amid the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2026 exercise being conducted by the Delhi Election Commission. Nearly 47.6 lakh names were removed from Delhi's draft electoral roll published on August 31, but only a fraction of those affected have so far submitted Form 6 seeking re-inclusion.The window for filing claims and objections against the draft roll will remain open until September 30.The draft electoral roll contains 97.5 lakh electors, compared with 1.45 crore registered voters in Delhi when the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise began in June.Data showed that 62,583 Form 6 applications, including those from first-time voters seeking inclusion, had been submitted by September 15. The number rose to 68,043 by September 16.The 47.6 lakh electors excluded from Delhi's draft electoral roll have been categorised as Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others following the house-to-house verification exercise. Around 43.3 lakh were marked as absent or shifted, while about 2.8 lakh were categorised as dead and 1.4 lakh as duplicate entries.According to figures released by the Delhi election office for the claims and objections phase, 91,826 applications were received between August 31 and September 16.These included 22,715 Form 8 applications seeking correction or modification of existing electoral entries, 922 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names on grounds such as death, shifting, duplicate registration or ineligibility, and 146 Form 6A applications from overseas electors, besides Form 6 applications for inclusion in the electoral roll.After the claims and objections phase ends, officials will examine the applications and complete the disposal process by October 29. The final electoral roll under the SIR exercise is scheduled to be published on November 4.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fear and anger in South Africa as bodies of nine women found: What we know
articles.summary: Police examining ‘all possibilities’ as women in Ekurhuleni, Johannesburg, fear murders could be linked.
articles.body:
The bodies of nine women have been found in South Africa’s Ekurhuleni municipality over the past two months, prompting police to investigate potential connections between the crimes.

The apparent murders, which bear similarities, have shaken the country, long plagued by high rates of crime and femicide and sparked fears that one or more offenders could strike again.

President Cyril Ramaphosa, who urged men to play a greater part in preventing violence against women and girls, has ordered the police to leave “no stone unturned” in their pursuit of justice.

The rate at which women are killed in South Africa is five times higher than the global average, according to figures from UN Women.

South African police made their latest discovery on Thursday, September 17 , when they found the body of a woman in Dawn Park on the outskirts of Johannesburg in Ekurhuleni municipality.

Local police said the unidentified, partially clothed woman, believed to be around 30, had been stabbed and dumped before being discovered.

Police said she may have been killed at another location before her body was moved to the park.

She is the ninth known woman to be killed in similar circumstances since July 17 .

All the murdered women were found in Ekurhuleni municipality in the greater Johannesburg area.

The first five bodies were found in the Kempton Park area. The others were found in separate locations 25-35km away.

Dawn Park, where the latest body was found, is about 30km south of Kempton Park.

Of the nine women whose bodies have been discovered, only four have been identified, according to local media.

The battered and burned body of Dineo Motapane, a 38-year-old mother of two, was discovered this week in a residential area of Ekurhuleni.

The body of 28-year-old Gracious Nkomo, also partially clothed, was found on September 10, having been dumped on the R21 highway in Kempton Park.

Last week, 38-year-old Elizabeth Moselakgomo was also found dead in Kempton Park. Local media reported that her young daughter alerted the police when she failed to return from a run.

Itumeleng Kekana, 32, was a shopkeeper. Her bruised and partially clothed body was found dumped on a bridge in July, 17 days after she was last seen by family members.

Five of the women have not yet been identified.

Police say they have not established whether the crimes are connected or if they were committed by one or more perpetrators.

However, police are probing potential links after noting similarities in the ages of the victims and the conditions in which they were found.

All are believed to have been in their 20s or 30s and some were found either naked or partially clothed, according to police. Some of the bodies also had similar bruising.

As local women voice fears of a serial killer, Fred Kekana, police commissioner of the Gauteng province where Ekurhuleni is , cautioned against hastily coming to conclusions.

“Investigators are considering all possibilities, including the possibility of multiple suspects or separate perpetrators,” said Kekana. “Police are comparing the evidence, timelines, locations, victim profiles and circumstances of each case before reaching conclusions.”

At least one suspect has been detained by police.

Deputy police commissioner Tebello Mosikili said the suspect appeared in court on Wednesday and would remain in custody. Police received information suggesting the suspect was not a South African national and were working to verify that, Mosikili said.

Acting national police commissioner Puleng Dimpane also said police were looking into a person of interest, but it was unclear whether she was referring to the same suspect.

Gauteng premier Panyaza Lesufi said whoever is responsible had effectively “declared war against the state” and expressed confidence that police would solve the case.

“We’ll get them,” he told South African media. “And I have trust in the law enforcement agencies.”

Police have urged the public to report any information they believe could assist the investigation and offered a reward of 400,000 rand ($25,000) for information leading to an arrest.

Police have also advised women in the area to be on heightened alert and to avoid walking or running alone near Kempton Park, where some of the bodies were found.

The National Shelter Movement of South Africa (NSMSA), which funds shelters for women and children affected by gender-based violence, said women already take extensive precautions for their safety and that authorities should not put the onus on women to prevent violence.

“Safety messaging should not imply that women can prevent violence simply by making different choices,” the organisation told Al Jazeera. “The responsibility for violence lies with perpetrators, while the responsibility for protection lies with society and the state.”

“We are not dealing with an issue of women who are not vigilant,” added Philisiwe Gabela, an official with the country’s Commission for Gender Equality.

President Ramaphosa last month called on men in South Africa to take a stand against gender-based violence and femicide by signing a virtual pledge.

He has argued that perpetrators of sexual assault and domestic violence are predominantly male, so men must hold each other accountable, challenge harmful patriarchal norms and report abuse of women to the police.

The killings have triggered widespread fear and anger about gender-based violence, which South Africa has one of the world’s highest rates of.

“I am feeling a lot of fear and paranoia, especially for ‌‌us ⁠⁠with daughters,” Ekurhuleni area resident Nomgqibelo Tshabalala told Reuters.

Between 2020 and 2021, an average of 5.5 out of 100,000 women in South Africa were killed by intimate partners, according to the South African Medical Research Council.

South African police recorded 9,782 reported rapes between January and March this year and 12,590 sexual offences. That amounts to roughly 108 reported rapes every day. It is widely known that many women do not report rape because of the fear of stigmatisation or reprisals.

Princess Eurika Mogane, a commissioner at South Africa’s Commission for Gender Equality, told Al Jazeera the latest killings reflect the broader crisis facing South African women. “This is a war. It feels like individuals are being hunted,” she said.

The UN South Africa said the killings are not “isolated tragedies”.

“They reflect the persistent and deadly violence faced by women and girls in South Africa.”

articles.title: Strange rock catches scientist's eye during creek search, leading to rare discovery
articles.summary: An Ice Age Pacific mastodon molar in immaculate condition was found in a San Mateo County creek, and scientists say the rest of the skeleton may still be buried there.
articles.body: A scientist surveying a California creek recently stumbled across something unexpected: a tooth from the mouth of an Ice Age giant. The discovery of the tooth, which belonged to an ancient Pacific mastodon, was announced by the Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District (Midpen) in San Mateo County, California. Mastodons were massive, elephant-like herbivores that went extinct roughly 11,700 years ago, near the end of the last Ice Age. SHOCKING PREHISTORIC DISCOVERY ON NJ BEACH '100%' CAME FROM COLOSSAL ANCIENT PREDATOR The tooth was found in a Midpen preserve creek by Brigid Lynch, a Balance Hydrologics geomorphologist who was surveying the area as part of an effort to improve the habitat of the threatened California red-legged frog. "As a geologist, I've gone out and seen stuff in the field, but definitely nothing as exciting as this," Lynch said in a release. Pictures of the molar show its strange shape, which Lynch initially thought was an oddly shaped rock. The tooth is in "immaculate condition," Wayne Thompson, CEO of Pacific Paleontology, told Fox News Digital in an interview. T REX FOOTPRINTS UNEARTHED IN FIRST-EVER DISCOVERY 66 MILLION YEARS AFTER CREATURE WALKED THE EARTH Thompson, whose job it was to examine the fossil and assess the site where it was discovered, said the tooth likely dates back between 50,000 and 100,000 years, based on where it was found. "It doesn't happen often. … [It's] quite uncommon." "There is a lot of misinformation going around about the age of the tooth," he said. "Most of the reports out [there] are saying it's 10,000 years old, but it's not 10,000 years. "From the location where the specimen was found, we can pretty confidently say that it’s much, much older than 11,700 years — probably on the order between 50 and 100,000 years," he added. ANCIENT OCEAN MYSTERY DEEPENS AS LONG-MISIDENTIFIED FOSSIL IS FINALLY REVEALED BY RESEARCHERS Thompson said the condition of the tooth also offers clues about what happened to it after the mastodon died, noting that it "hadn't moved very much in the stream where the creature died." "Mastodon teeth are — the roots are extremely fragile — and this one had the majority of the roots of the molar still preserved with it intact, and so, it wasn't tumbled around in the stream," he said. The paleontologist believes the rest of the animal may still be at the site. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "It probably recently came out of the skull and the skull, along with the rest of the bones, are still buried out there," he said. It is "extremely rare" to find a mastodon molar in such well-preserved condition, Thompson said. "It doesn't happen often. ... [It's] quite uncommon," he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Looking ahead, researchers from Stanford University's Doerr School of Sustainability plan to carbon date the molar to determine its exact age. Researchers will also create a 3-D scan of the tooth, which will be used to produce a replica. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Thompson said mastodons favored creek and river valleys, browsing on leaves rather than grazing on grasses as mammoths did. Alder trees, he said, were among their preferred food sources — and they still line the creek where the tooth was found. articles.title: A 72-year-old Scottish gran thought she’d won a horse, then discovered her £15 ticket had won her a £4 million Cornwall mansion, mortgage-free, plus £250,000 cash and £200,000 worth of furnishings
articles.summary: UK News: A 72-year-old grandmother from Scotland was left stunned after initially believing she had won a horse, only to discover that she had actually scooped.
articles.body: A 72-year-old grandmother from Scotland was left stunned after initially believing she had won a horse, only to discover that she had actually scooped a £4 million coastal mansion in Cornwall with a £15 Omaze entry.Mary Dickson, from Castle Douglas in south-west Scotland, almost missed out on the life-changing prize after ignoring calls from unknown numbers. When Omaze eventually contacted her and took her to a reveal location, she was even more confused when the first thing she saw was a horse standing in a field.‘I said thanks but no thanks!’Recalling the unusual moment, Mary was quoted as saying by SWNS, “The first thing I saw when I turned the corner was a horse. I said thanks but no thanks! Then I realised I’d actually won a house, not a horse, so I quickly said thank you very much!”Mary had entered the Omaze draw as part of her subscription, paying just £15 for the chance to win the four-bedroom property near the fishing village of Coverack in Cornwall.The grandmother said she nearly missed the call confirming her win because she had no mobile signal and generally does not answer calls from numbers she does not recognise.“I ignored Omaze’s calls at first. But they texted me, so I checked them out online, they looked like the real deal, so I thought I’d better call back. Thank goodness I did!” she said.“All the family came to see the reveal, I was gobsmacked when they told me it was the house.”The family later headed to a pub to celebrate, although Mary opted for coffee rather than an alcoholic drink.“Although I’m looking forward to a glass of wine by my new pool,” she added.Four-bedroom mansion comes mortgage-freeMary and her husband John, 76, will receive the property mortgage-free, with stamp duty and legal fees covered. The prize also includes £250,000 in cash and £200,000 worth of furnishings.The couple, who have lived in a terrace house in Castle Douglas since 2000, say they are in no hurry to decide what they will ultimately do with their new home.“We’re going to keep it for a while and just enjoy it and we can’t wait to host Christmas here with all the family,” Mary said.The property boasts panoramic sea views and direct access to Porthbeer Cove. Designed around its coastal setting, the house features floor-to-ceiling windows and four double bedrooms, three of which have dressing rooms and en-suite bathrooms.The first floor includes an open-plan kitchen, dining and living area, along with a study, conservatory, boot room and utility room.Outside, the expansive grounds feature a heated swimming pool with a swim-up bar, sunken banquette seating and a fire pit. There is also an outdoor kitchen with a barbecue and pizza oven, landscaped gardens and a private driveway leading to a three-car garage.Despite the property having stables, Mary has made it clear that the couple are not planning to add horse ownership to their list of new commitments.‘There must be something in the water up here’Mary began entering Omaze draws after a colleague won an Omaze house in the Lake District in 2023.“When I saw that he’d won, it made me realise real people really do win these houses - I did wonder if he’d used up all the luck around here, but it must’ve rubbed off on me,” she said.“There must be something in the water up here.”Mary said she texted her colleague after discovering her own win because he was “the only person I knew who could possibly know how I was feeling”.The couple last visited Cornwall around 20 years ago, when they travelled along the coast and stayed in hotels. They never imagined their next visit would involve viewing their own multimillion-pound home.“We never imagined that when we next came back to Cornwall, it would be to see our very own £4million mansion. It’s absolutely stunning, we just can’t believe it’s all ours,” Mary said.“Our house in Scotland could probably fit on the turning circle on our new driveway.”She also joked about the journey south, referencing Scottish band The Proclaimers.“Funnily enough, The Proclaimers popped up on the telly promoting their new album the morning we went to see the house for the first time - fitting really, as we gladly went 500 miles to arrive at this door!”A win that will change the family’s futureJohn spent 27 years working as a draughtsman at a Motherwell steelworks before moving into an IT role with the fire and rescue service. He retired in 2011.The couple have been together since 1996 and married in 2017. Mary has two daughters, one of whom has sadly passed away. They remain close to her late daughter’s two sons, aged 17 and 22.Mary said the win would have a lasting impact on the entire family.“This win is fantastic for all our family, we’ll enjoy it together for now, and owning such a valuable property is life-changing for all of us,” she said.Cornwall property sits near Porthbeer CoveThe mansion is located on the Lizard Peninsula, on the eastern side of the Cornwall National Landscape. Porthbeer Cove, a sheltered sandy beach, is a short walk away along the South West Coast Path.Falmouth, known for its harbourside restaurants and galleries, is around 30 minutes away, while Redruth is the nearest mainline railway station, offering direct services to London Paddington.Mary won the property through an Omaze draw conducted in partnership with Wellbeing of Women. According to Omaze, the draw guaranteed £1 million for the charity, while the company also committed a further £3.5 million through a separate multi-year grant.Matt Pohlson, founder and CEO of Omaze, said the company was “over the moon” that Mary and John had won the Cornwall property while supporting Wellbeing of Women.“Omaze offers people the chance to win incredible prizes, whilst also introducing charities to new audiences that they wouldn’t normally reach - it’s a win-win for entrants and our charity partners,” he said.The company said the Omaze community has raised more than £150 million for good causes across the UK.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Converse pulls 'deeply upsetting' advert after backlash
articles.summary: Social media users say an image from the brand's Instagram account resembled a KKK hood and hanging.
articles.body:
American footwear brand Converse has pulled an advert that social media users said evoked Ku Klux Klan imagery, saying it recognised "that we got this wrong".

The photo, posted to the company's Instagram account, received backlash online after critics described lighting in the image as looking like a white pointed hood.

A pair of shoes, dangling in the picture, were also likened to an image of a lynching victim by social media users.

In an apology, first issued on Friday, Converse said the photo had been removed from its social media channels and it was working to remove it elsewhere. "This should not have happened and we will do better," it said.

The statement also said: "We're sorry. We understand why this image is deeply upsetting and recognize that we got this wrong".

The photo was part of a campaign promoting its Chuck 70 X trainer, launched internationally on 27 August.

The campaign features the South Korean singer Karina, of the K-pop group Aespa, who is pictured in a series of advertisements for the shoes.

Founded in Massachusetts in the early 1900s, the popularity of Converse has skyrocketed since its Chuck Taylor sneaker was first introduced to US basketball courts in 1917.

The global brand has been a subsidiary of Nike since 2003.

articles.title: The week Gainesville forgot about football: Inside the terror that gripped Florida during the 1990 murders
articles.summary: UF alumni recall the terror of Danny Rolling's 1990 murder spree and how Steve Spurrier's home opener against Oklahoma State restored normalcy.
articles.body: College football season in Gainesville is everything. Everything. The town has forever revolved around the Florida Gators. Gainesville is a college town. It's built around the university. As the program goes, so does the town. With all due respect to Miami and FSU, most would argue that Florida is a Gators state. Yes, I know that'll ruffle some feathers. Let's not get caught up on that, please. Just bear with me. My point? Very few things in life can actually take attention away from the Florida Gators during football season — especially with a legend like Steve Spurrier set to return home, this time as the program's head coach. August of 1990 did just that. HOW A PODCAST COMMUNITY HELPED RESTORE THE CONTROVERSIAL 'GATOR BAIT' CHANT FOR FLORIDA FOOTBALL TEAM "I remember at Walmart, the gun line was down the aisle," former UF student Erik Tallbacka told OutKick this week. "When a hurricane's coming, and you're at Home Depot and preparing, there's that kind of electricity, like something's coming. And it was that hurricane sensation. "But it wasn't a hurricane's coming. It was people getting killed every night, for three nights in a row. The whole campus, the whole town, just had that palpable feeling of 'everybody's in this together.'" Florida alumni relive the Gainesville murders Earlier this week, I wrote about ESPN's recent 30 for 30 on Danny Rolling, also known as the "Gainesville Ripper." Rolling brutally murdered five students in August 1990 — days before Labor Day weekend and roughly two weeks before the start of a new football season. Rolling was eventually arrested, pled guilty to the murders — along with several in Shreveport, Louisiana — and was later sentenced to death. He died via lethal injection in 2006. Rolling became known as the "Gainesville Ripper." His killing spree, which had no real motive, led to several books, and one movie. The horror franchise "Scream" is loosely based on the Gainesville Murders, according to the screenwriter Kevin Williamson. So, yes — 36 years later, that infamous week is still fresh one everyone's minds. You don't simply live through that and forget, you know? I had dozens of readers reach out to me after I wrote about it on Wednesday — most of them UF alumni who were on campus while Rolling was at large. The word they all used? Horrific. "You could drive down the road or through apartment complexes and people had braces in their windows to keep someone from opening them," remembered Duane Engel. "No one had any clue who was involved." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Of course, there was no social media, either. This was decades before X. Tallbacka said you watched the nightly news for any new information, and that was all you got. Everyone was on edge. "As you walked around town and campus, I remember, if you're going into a store, just looking at everybody, like it could be any guy," he recalled. "And we just had no idea. When you'd go to bed at night, especially by the third day, when there'd been five murders, I mean, that night, you're wondering, is somebody going to break into my apartment? "And so sleeping was weird. I was living with a couple other guys, my girlfriend was living with a couple girls, and we were sleeping over there. And like I mentioned, we didn't have guns. I was a big hunter, but didn't have any guns in college. But we had brought golf clubs and baseball bats and we were sleeping on the couch. Any noise that you heard, you know, a car door slamming, you were just so on edge." Spurrier famously allowed the girlfriends of players to sleep in Yon Hall — a high-security complex where the entire football team lived. Matt Sovic had just returned to campus for his senior year, and attended a party the weekend the murders began. He was staying with friends at Williamsburg Village — the same complex where freshmen Sonja Larson and Christina Powell lived. "I parked my car directly in front of the of the door to the four units that contained the residence of the first victims," he said. "As we left to go party that Saturday night, when my old roommate entered my car he tossed his beer can out of my window and into the yard. "The next day we watched as it was placed into an evidence bag. I can guarantee you that beer in the evidence bag was a tall boy Budweiser. Not knowing yet there was a double murder, we jokingly told our friend he was a suspect for whatever happened now that they had his prints." Florida football returns, injects hope into Gainesville Rolling murdered five students from Aug. 24 to Aug. 27. Four of them were females with brunette hair and brown eyes, the same as his mother. The fifth was 23-year-old Manny Taboada — a 6-foot-2, 200-pound male. "It wasn’t until we found out he killed that massive guy, who worked on the corner of Acher and I think 34th, that all the egos took a fall on campus," remembered Kevin Letize, who was just starting his senior year. "We all thought it was a typical perv killer until that came out. "Once the big kid was killed, all the 'tough' students took it much more seriously." So, how does football fit into all of this? Well, it really doesn't — beyond, perhaps, a much-needed bookend to the most terrifying week in the history of the town. After much discussion, Florida, and Spurrier, kicked off the new season Sept. 8 against Oklahoma State. The murders had stopped, at least for a few days, but a lot of students had left for good by then. The ones who stayed did their best to get back to some sort of normalcy. The Gators won, 50-7. Shane Matthews instantly became a household name. Spurrier had revived Florida football. More importantly, the team had revived a town in desperate need of a reason to smile. "I've never seen a place so terrorized," said Glenn Summers. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Added Tallbacka: "I guess everybody was in a fog. But I think by the time that game happened, it had been over a week since anybody been killed. And I do think, in retrospect, watching that game brought everybody back to normalcy. It wasn't just going to class and classes are canceled. And every night for three nights, somebody has been killed. "By the time a week went by, by the time the football game happened, I think that must have been when everybody finally relaxed. I think that was the conclusion."

articles.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger helped protect 240,000 acres of California ranchland; the vast habitat is home to rare species and condors
articles.summary: US News: On May 8, 2008, California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger joined Tejon Ranch Company and five major environmental organisations to announce a landmark.
articles.body: On May 8, 2008, California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger joined Tejon Ranch Company and five major environmental organisations to announce a landmark conservation and land-use agreement covering the 270,000-acre Tejon Ranch. The agreement was designed to permanently protect up to 240,000 acres, roughly 90% of the ranch, while allowing limited development and continued ranching and other historical activities on the remaining land. The deal followed about two years of negotiations between Tejon Ranch Company and Audubon California, the Endangered Habitats League, the Natural Resources Defense Council, the Planning and Conservation League and the Sierra Club. Schwarzenegger supported and publicly announced the agreement, but the negotiations themselves were conducted between the company and the environmental organisations. The agreement created the independent Tejon Ranch Conservancy and established a framework for conservation, management and public access across the enormous property. Tejon Ranch Company has described the pact as the largest private conservation agreement in California history.A meeting point of four ecological regionsTejon Ranch stretches across parts of Kern and Los Angeles counties and occupies an unusual position where several major ecological regions meet. The agreement documents describe the property as lying at the confluence of the Sierra Nevada, Mojave Desert, Coastal Range and San Joaquin Valley, creating a landscape with an unusually broad range of habitats and plant communities. The ranch contains native grasslands, oak woodlands, Joshua tree woodlands and conifer forests, as well as intact watersheds and habitat corridors.The property's ecological importance was one of the central reasons for the conservation negotiations. The joint statement announcing the agreement described Tejon Ranch as habitat for the California condor and more than two dozen other rare plant and animal species. Species specifically identified in conservation materials include the San Joaquin kit fox, blunt-nosed leopard lizard and Tehachapi slender salamander. The Tejon Ranch Conservancy now says more than 60 at-risk plant and animal species are protected on the ranch. The size of the property also mattered. At about 422 square miles, Tejon Ranch is the largest contiguous private landholding in California, according to the Conservancy. Its large, relatively unfragmented landscape allows habitats to remain connected across mountains, grasslands, forests and desert environments.The agreement protected 178,000 acres firstThe headline figure of 240,000 acres requires some explanation. Under the agreement signed on June 17, 2008, Tejon Ranch Company committed to the phased dedication of conservation easements covering approximately 178,000 acres. The environmental organisations were also given options to acquire conservation easements over five additional areas totalling approximately 62,000 acres. If those options were exercised, the conserved area would reach about 240,000 acres.The agreement therefore did not simply transfer 240,000 acres to a conservation organisation in 2008. Instead, it established a long-term legal and financial framework for conserving the ranch while allowing the company to continue certain activities. The company's SEC filing said existing revenue-producing activities, including farming, ranching and oil and mineral extraction, could continue on conserved lands where permitted under the agreement. At the same time, the arrangement allowed the company to pursue entitlement and development processes for specified projects on the remainder of the ranch. The structure was intended to replace years of potential conflict between conservation and development interests with a negotiated framework. In return for the conservation commitments, the participating environmental organisations agreed not to oppose certain specified development projects, including Tejon Mountain Village and Centennial, subject to the applicable regulatory processes.The Tejon Ranch Conservancy became the land's independent stewardThe agreement also created the Tejon Ranch Conservancy, an independent nonprofit organisation responsible for conservation planning and management of the conserved lands. Its mission is to preserve, enhance and restore the ranch's native biodiversity and ecosystem values. The Conservancy says it now oversees conservation planning, protection and management across the 240,000 acres of conserved Tejon Ranch land.Public access was another component of the agreement. The SEC filing says the pact guaranteed significant public access to conserved areas through a public access plan developed by the Conservancy. One provision called for the realignment of 37 miles of the Pacific Crest Trail across approximately 10,000 acres through the heart of the ranch. The agreement also called for docent-led tours of Bear Trap Canyon and cooperation with state officials on the possibility of creating a major state park covering nearly 50,000 acres. The Conservancy's present-day work includes research, habitat protection, restoration, grazing management, invasive-species control and public education. It also facilitates opportunities for visitors to experience parts of the ranch through organised public-access programmes.Schwarzenegger announced the deal, but did not negotiate itSchwarzenegger's role in the agreement was significant but should be described accurately. His own environmental record says that on May 8, 2008, he announced a historic agreement between the Tejon Ranch landowners and conservation and environmental groups that would give California its largest-ever privately conserved parcel. At the announcement, he praised the agreement as an example of environmental protection being pursued alongside economic development.The negotiations, however, were conducted by Tejon Ranch Company and the five participating environmental organisations. Tejon's own announcement said the discussions had evolved into about two years of formal negotiations, while the company's later Governor's Environmental and Economic Leadership Award announcement specifically recognised Tejon executives for their leadership in negotiating the agreement. The agreement was formally signed on June 17, 2008, and the Tejon Ranch Conservancy was established as part of the arrangement. The result was a long-term conservation framework covering roughly 90% of one of California's largest private landscapes, while leaving the company with defined opportunities for development and continued working-ranch activities on other parts of the property.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: MS NOW journalists denied entry to White House after Trump announces ban
articles.summary: US News: A day after US President Donald Trump announced a ban on MS NOW, CNN and Politico from the White House, journalists from MS NOW were denied access to .
articles.body: A day after US President Donald Trump announced a ban on MS NOW, CNN and Politico from the White House, journalists from MS NOW were denied access to the White House grounds on Saturday.MS NOW reporter Akayla Gardner said her White House press badge was disabled when she arrived Saturday morning. A security officer asked her to hand over the badge and told her that the decision was “above him”.A photographer from the network was also denied access, while one of its producers was allowed onto the White House grounds. It was not immediately clear why their access differed.MS NOW said the White House belongs to the American people and that the network would take “any and all steps necessary” to defend its First Amendment rights and the role of independent journalists in a democracy.Why did Trump ban MS NOW, CNN, Politico?Trump announced the ban on Friday, accusing the three outlets of repeatedly reporting what he called “FAKE NEWS”. In a Truth Social post, he said media organisations “shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES” while covering the president.Asked about the decision in the Oval Office, Trump said it was based on “cumulative stories over the last few years”. He did not identify any specific report that prompted the ban. Trump also warned that other news organisations could face similar action.CNN said it stood behind its White House team and its “fair and accurate reporting”. Politico rejected Trump's claim that it had received government subsidies, saying the allegation had been “thoroughly debunked”, and said it would defend its First Amendment rights.Trump’s wider media fightThe latest move comes amid Trump's broader clashes with news organisations over their coverage of his administration. Earlier, his administration restricted Associated Press access to certain White House spaces after the news agency declined to use the administration's preferred name for the Gulf of Mexico.Trump has also taken legal action against several media organisations, including the BBC, The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal, accusing them of defamation. The disputes have further intensified tensions between the Trump administration and sections of the US media.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lib Dems will be a firewall against Nigel Farage, Davey says
articles.summary: Lib Dem leader Ed Davey claimed the party was aiming to beat its 2024 record of 72 MPs in any snap election.
articles.body:
Sir Ed Davey said the Liberal Democrats are "a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform" as the party's conference began in Brighton.

The Lib Dem leader sought to strike a more combative stance as he faced down criticism from his own MPs that the party was struggling for relevance and being too polite about problems.

On the first day of the autumn conference, Sir Ed warned an "unholy alliance" between Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch and Farage could turn the UK into a "Trump satellite state".

Addressing speculation about a possible snap election, he said the party was ready to fight and would build its so-called orange wall even higher by winning more than its 2024 record of 72 MPs.

Sir Ed's attention-grabbing stunts helped raise the party's profile ahead of the last election, but recent polling showed 43% of respondents were unclear what the Liberal Democrats stand for, with just over half describing them as "weak".

South Cotswolds MP Roz Savage criticised Sir Ed's leadership ahead of conference, urging the party to rediscover its "insurgent spirit" rather than being the "polite custodians of a system that leaves people feeling powerless".

Speaking on the pebbles of Brighton Beach, Sir Ed dismissed those concerns and told reporters the Liberal Democrats would fight to stop a Reform government.

"One of the things that makes us unique is that we are a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform," he said.

"Many of the seats he needs to get himself into No 10 are seats that we will defend and indeed win - and we are also able to take seats off the Conservatives, because I really fear that Kemi Badenoch will give the keys to No 10 to Nigel Farage, so we have got to stop the Conservatives as well.

"We have got an historic opportunity to win many more seats and a moral responsibility to stop Reform."

He added a manifesto working group had already been set up in case of an early election "so we'll be ready if it comes early, but, you know, it still could be up to three years away".

Sir Ed insisted his party has a "distinctive position" in British politics, and will use the four-day conference to position it to take on the challenge from Reform as well as its typical rivals the Conservatives, talking up their focus on the NHS and goal of re-joining the EU single market and customs union.

The Lib Dem leader highlighted how six former Conservative cabinet ministers were among 25 Tories to have defected to Reform in the last two years, claiming they were now competing with each other to see who can divide the country more, rather than looking to fix the country's problems.

"An unholy alliance between Farage and Badenoch is the only way either can get into power," he said.

"Together, they want to turn Britain into a Trump satellite state which would trash our NHS, turn our communities against each other, cause untold damage to our environment, and trample over traditional British values of fairness, tolerance, and decency.

"A bigger Orange Wall is the only thing that can stand between Britain and this dangerous experiment, and we will not let them pass."

Davey also attacked the Labour government as having no plan for growth, failing to support families struggling with the cost of living and taxing small businesses "to the brink".

Ahead of a speech to party members, Davey urged Liberal Democrats not to look away from injustice or "human dignity under attack" but to fight back.

articles.title: 'We want to go home': Hindu minor sisters abducted, converted, married in Pakistan's Sindh
articles.summary: Pakistan News: The alleged abduction and forced conversion of two minor Hindu sisters in Pakistan's Sindh province has triggered fresh concern among minority rights .
articles.body: The alleged abduction and forced conversion of two minor Hindu sisters in Pakistan's Sindh province has triggered fresh concern among minority rights group, with one organisation calling for an independent probe and safeguards for the girls.According to Voice of Pakistan Minority, Roopi, 13 and Seeta, 14, were allegedly taken from Ibrahim Colony in Tando Allahyar district and later converted to Islam and married to two Muslim men, Amjad Solangi and Mansood Solangi.The sisters were subsequently brought before a court in Tando Allahyar in an abduction case. Instead of sending them back to their family, the court placed them in a safe house, VOPM said.The rights group said the girls appeared distressed outside the court and were heard pleading to be taken home. A video circulating online also purportedly showed the sisters saying, “Let us go to our parents” and “We want to go home.”VOPM said the circumstances surrounding the case made it important that the sisters be heard independently, without anyone who could influence or intimidate them.“The state must interview Roopi and Seeta in a child-sensitive environment, away from alleged husbands, religious figures, intermediaries or anyone who could pressure them. Officials must allow the girls to speak freely and must provide them independent legal support and protection,” VOPM said.The organisation called for an urgent, independent and transparent investigation into the allegations.Sindh at centre of concern over minority girlsThe case has also renewed attention on the vulnerability of Hindu families in Sindh, which has Pakistan's largest Hindu population. VOPM said the problem is particularly acute in rural areas, where poverty, caste discrimination and limited access to legal assistance can leave minority families vulnerable.“This case has caused deep anxiety among Hindu communities in Sindh. Sindh hosts Pakistan’s largest Hindu population, particularly in rural districts where many Hindu families face poverty, caste discrimination and weak access to legal help,” it said.Rights groups have for years raised concerns over allegations involving the abduction, conversion and marriage of minority girls in Pakistan.VOPM cited data from the Centre for Social Justice, included in UK government material, which recorded 421 such cases involving minority girls and women between 2021 and 2024. Hindu women and girls accounted for 282 of those cases, while 72 per cent were reported from Sindh.The organisation said Pakistani authorities recorded at least 83 cases in 2024 alone, with Hindu girls making up 63 per cent of the victims.The concern extends beyond the figures. VOPM also referred to warnings by UN experts in 2026 that nearly 80 per cent of reported cases involving alleged forced conversion through marriage in Pakistan during 2025 took place in Sindh. About 75 per cent of the victims were reportedly Hindus.For VOPM, the immediate focus remains on the two sisters and whether they can speak freely about what happened to them.“Roopi and Seeta’s reported call to return home demands attention. Their protection, age, dignity, and freedom must come before every other consideration,” the VOPM noted.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: A 77-year-old Walmart shopper died after he was allegedly attacked by the parents of a teenage store employee following an argument over a shopping cart in Norfolk, Virginia.Bert Atienza died of blunt head trauma on June 8, a day after he was attacked inside a Walmart store, according to WTKR. His death was ruled a homicide.Atienza was shopping with his wife Josephine after attending church when a 17-year-old Walmart employee allegedly rushed down an aisle with a cart and nearly hit her.Josephine told WTKR that her husband confronted the teenager, saying she had almost hit his wife and had not apologised.The couple then continued shopping after a brief argument with the employee. Josephine alleged that the teenager threw a can towards them before leaving the area and calling her parents.Elderly shopper attacked inside WalmartMinutes later, Travis White, 44, and Erika Mitchell, 42, allegedly tracked down the couple inside the store and attacked Atienza, according to surveillance footage obtained by WTKR.The footage shows Atienza being shoved, grabbed and punched before he was pushed into a shelf and fell to the floor. One of the suspects allegedly kicked him while he was down.“They crowded my husband, one of the adults hit him in the face. He fell down on the floor. articles.title: Film by Bournemouth student scoops international awards
articles.summary: First-year student Tommy Balmont's film Hemophobia is a psychological drama about a young vampire.
articles.body:
A first-year university student has celebrated international success with a short film about a young vampire.

Hemophobia was written and directed by Tommy Balmont while he was studying for a BA in film production at Arts University Bournemouth (AUB).

The short film premiered in June, going on to win Best Student Film at the London Independent Film Awards and the New York Film and Actress Awards.

The film follows a young vampire's descent into an addiction to blood and the impact it has on the relationship with her human girlfriend.

Balmont created the film as part of the course's first year storytelling module, alongside Toby Wild-Pearmain as first assistant director.

Wild-Pearmain said: "When we set out to make Hemophobia, our main focus was bringing Tommy's unique script to life and pushing ourselves creatively.

"To see it premiere locally at the Palace Court Theatre and then go on to win awards in London and New York has been an incredible experience."

Now listed on IMDb, the film has been selected for consideration by five international festivals, alongside an invitation to screen at the Vesuvio International Movie Awards in Italy.

Dean of Bournemouth Film School at AUB, Tim Metcalf, said: "For a first-year project to achieve this level of international recognition so early on is a fantastic testament to the talent and dedication of our students.

"Hemophobia demonstrates exactly what Bournemouth Film School is all about – bold storytelling, technical precision and a commitment to compelling filmmaking.

"We are immensely proud of Tommy, Toby and the entire team, and we look forward to following the film's progress as it continues its festival journey."

articles.title: FBI warned immigration authorities about fake tradwife dating profiles
articles.summary: An FBI memo said that a small group of women were posing with a “traditional wife” esthetic as a tactic to lure immigration authorities.
articles.body: The FBI warned immigration officers internally that a group of women were creating fake online dating profiles with tradwife aesthetics to lure and dox them. The FBI’s Chicago field office distributed a memo in February warning the country’s law enforcement agencies that a small group of women were creating the fake accounts in January targeting immigration authorities. The dating profiles were “incorporating imagery of a ‘traditional wife’ aesthetic and listing specific interests in an attempt to appeal to an individuals in law enforcement,” according to the memo. “The objective was to lure affiliated law enforcement personnel into an online or in-person interaction under the guise of a date, after which the individuals would be publicly exposed and doxed online,” the memo reads. “The tactic is intended to generate public embarrassment and deter immigration enforcement activity.” NBC News was provided the memo by Property of the People, a nonprofit organization focused on government transparency, which obtained it through a state open records request. The memo was first reported by The Guardian. The FBI confirmed the authenticity of the memo to NBC News. “While our standard practice is to not comment on specific intelligence products, the FBI regularly shares information with our law enforcement partners to assist in protecting the communities they serve as well as protecting those who serve and protect communities,” the agency said in a statement. “The FBI is committed to ensuring that law enforcement officers are safe from threats or violence while performing their duties.” The memo did not state where the dating profiles were created or share examples of what the profiles contained. It was sent amid a surge of thousands of immigration officers to the Twin Cities, dubbed by the federal government as “Operation Metro Surge.” The effort was ramped down after the fatal shootings of two U.S. citizens, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, who were protesting immigration enforcement in Minneapolis in January. The immigration crackdown and killings prompted sweeping protests across the country and national furor against federal law enforcement. The alleged dating profiles in Chicago were also created several months after an immigration enforcement surge there known as “Operation Midway Blitz.”

articles.title: Demonstrators in US form human chain to protest Kennedy Center closure vote
articles.summary: ‘Hands Around the Kennedy Center’ rally drew thousands after Trump-backed board votes to close the iconic arts venue.
articles.body:
Thousands of protesters formed a human chain around the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington DC to contest its closure, amid fears that United States President Donald Trump could make good on his threat to demolish the venerated landmark.

The crowd filled streets in the Foggy Bottom neighbourhood of the capital on Friday evening, bringing traffic to a standstill as demonstrators made their way to the “Hands Around the Kennedy Center” protest. Many carried signs and some wore costumes, while boos rang out when Trump was mentioned during the programme.

At one point, some protesters linked hands around the building, whose marble facade remained partly concealed by scaffolding and tarpaulins.

Among the most iconic buildings on Washington’s Potomac waterfront, the Kennedy Center has become a battleground over Trump’s bid to assert control over the institution since he returned to office last year, replacing its board with his own appointees and installing himself as chairman.

Chris Raleigh, co-founder of Hands Off the Arts, which organised the rally, said in an interview with The Associated Press news agency that he hoped the turnout would show that people were prepared to push back against Trump’s plans for the building.

The demonstration comes just days after the Trump-installed board voted to close the centre for repairs that are expected to last up to two years. That came hours after District Judge Christopher Cooper quashed the board’s latest attempt to restore Trump’s name to the building.

Last December, the new board added Trump’s name to the building’s facade after the Kennedy Center said its Board of Trustees had unanimously voted to rename the institution in his honour.

A federal judge blocked those efforts in May, ruling that the board had exceeded its statutory authority by unilaterally renaming the Kennedy Center and adding Trump’s name to its facade without congressional approval. Congress had designated the centre as a memorial to the late 35th US President John F Kennedy.

In August, the board tried again to inscribe Trump’s name on the building, this time with wording along the lines of “The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts Restored and Renovated By President Donald J. Trump”.

The federal judge scotched the move in September, ruling that it violated his May injunction.

Trump has since declined to rule out demolishing the building, while a federal judge on Thursday ordered the Kennedy Center to give 30 days’ notice before undertaking any major structural changes, including demolition.

Speaking to reporters in North Carolina on Wednesday, Trump argued that his administration deserved recognition for rescuing the Kennedy Center and that without the repairs, the building risked falling into disrepair and ultimately being forced to shut down.

Raleigh said he, like others, is concerned that Trump could move ahead without first notifying the court.

“Look at the East Wing,” he said. “We got up one morning and there was a giant hole there.”

articles.title: In 2015, a Connecticut carpenter and his wife bought 5 acres in upstate New York for $27,000; he built three cabins, and the rentals generated more than $2.1 million
articles.summary: US News: When Chris Broomfield, 51, a Connecticut carpenter, and his wife bought 5 acres of land in upstate New York, he already knew what he was going to do w.
articles.body: When Chris Broomfield, 51, a Connecticut carpenter, and his wife bought 5 acres of land in upstate New York, he already knew what he was going to do with the property. They bought the land in 2015 for $27,000. Eight years later, the rental cabins he built on that land had generated more than $2.1 million in revenue! Something that began as a weekend project to give his children a financial head start became a thriving hospitality business, a million-dollar business serving Airbnb guests across the region.How a carpenter built a cabin empireChris Broomfield had spent decades doing carpentry contracting work. But there was a problem with passing that legacy forward. "Carpentry is a knowledge- and experience-based [business]," he told CNBC Make It. "I couldn't really hand that down to my kids. So I needed to build something that at least would give them a head start on something to borrow against or something that creates additional income." That's how it began.In 2015, he bought a five-acre property in Remsen, New York. The land was close to the place where he grew up. His brother also had a property nearby. He saw potential in those rolling hills and the property's proximity to the lake. He thought multiple short-term rental cabins could bring visitors.Broomfield began commuting eight hours every weekend from his Connecticut home to build an A-frame cabin largely by himself.“I always knew it was going to be an Airbnb property. I knew I was going to put multiple cabins on it. I chose this property because it was close to the lake. It was very wooded, and it had rolling hills. I saw its potential with multiple cabins,” he said.Three years into the process, he had completed a one-bedroom structure that would become his flagship property. The build cost roughly $90,000, though he hired outside help for specialised tasks such as drilling the well and handling electrical work. Broomfield's wife inspired a feature that guests couldn't stop photographing: a motorised king bed that slides out into the woods, letting renters sleep under the open sky. Along with it came a full kitchen, fireplace, fire pit and multiple decks. They listed the cabin for $60 a night on Airbnb. When demand spiked, the price went up to between $380 and $700 a night. By 2024, the A-frame was pulling in $119,337 annually, with 2025 projections near $143,500.“The process was amazing for me. I loved being up here. I loved being able to build anything that I wanted to build. Something that came from my mind and not a blueprint. The free rein was really enjoyable,” Broomfield told the publication.More cabinsOnce the A-frame cabin went viral, Broomfield moved quickly into his next project: a treehouse cabin. This time, he hired a team rather than doing it alone. Thirteen weeks later, in November 2019, the treehouse was finished. The treehouse, sitting 14 feet up, quickly grabbed attention. Guests had to cross a suspension bridge to reach it. Two bedrooms, a private pond with a dock, a covered porch and a living room overlooking a waterfall attracted families. In 2024, it generated $151,966 in revenue and ranked in Airbnb's top 10% by ratings and reviews.Broomfield knew this was his true calling. He started building more. In 2021, he completed the Birch Falls Spa Cabin, a studio featuring an 18-foot indoor waterfall, massage bed and soaker jet tub. The $160,000 structure brought in $120,227 that year.The monthly operating costs for the three cabins are about $8,000 in payroll and staff costs. Property taxes add $18,000 annually. Utilities run $700 a month. Against those expenses, Broomfield now pulls in roughly $400,000 a year! By September 2025, the cabins had earned him $2.1 million since the first one was listed for rent in 2018.Broomfield has no plans to stop. Two more cabins were built: Tiny house, and 2-story container cabin. “There’s always going to be something that is going to be pushing me to do the next thing. I can’t sit back and do nothing. My family is a huge part of my inspiration and my drive; eventually, they are going to be the ones owning this,” he told the outlet. What started as a head start for his kids now became a family business. “The legacy of Evergreen is, I don’t really have a plan for it [but] I do know that it is going to inspire and help people. My kids are going to be a part of that.”Now, Broomfield’s day-to-day consists of overseeing his staff, designing new cabins and developing future plans for Evergreen Cabins.Since retiring, Broomfield says it’s important for him to keep busy and keep building for his family.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: MUMBAI: The probe in the abetment of suicide case of an IIT-Bombay student was transferred to the Mumbai Police's crime branch late on Saturday.An ACP-rank officer from the crime branch will be carrying out the probe.Sahil Wakode, 20, was found dead in his hostel room at the campus on Friday.After his parents lodged a complaint with the Powai Police on Saturday, an FIR was registered for abetment of suicide under provisions of Bhartiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police also applied provisions of the Prevention of Atrocities Act, after Wakode's parents complained that he was being harassed with "casteist slurs."The FIR names a senior professor of IIT Bombay besides "other senior officials."This is the third incident of suicide on the campus this year.Wakode’s parents, Ravindra, an office-bearer with a multipurpose cooperative society, and Sonali, a govt school teacher, refused to claim their son’s body from the post-mortem centre at Rajawadi Hospital for over seven hours on Saturday.“I will not conduct the final rites of my son till the accused persons are arrested,” said Ravindra.Wakode was their only child. articles.title: Ed Sheeran concert set to go ahead after outcry over Gaza
articles.summary: Sheeran may perform solo after musicians dropped out of tour over expulsion of Macklemore for supporting Palestine.
articles.body:
Ed Sheeran is expected to return to the stage for the first time since the expulsion of Macklemore from his United States tour due to the rapper’s comments on stage in support of Palestine.

The decision provoked a backlash and prompted the rest of Sheeran’s opening acts to pull out .

Sheeran is scheduled to perform on Saturday at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. He may sing alone since the other opening acts dropped out in support of Macklemore and Gaza.

Finneas, the brother and collaborator of popular artist Billie Eilish, was originally scheduled to perform with Sheeran in some cities, but dropped out earlier this week. Danish band Lukas Graham and Irish singer Aaron Rowe were also supposed to open at various points on Sheeran’s global tour, but they also announced they would not perform.

Palestinian advocacy groups have called for a boycott of the tour, saying Sheeran is complicit in an effort to stifle criticism of Israel over its genocidal war in Gaza.

“We now extend our call for boycotting Ed Sheeran’s entire world tour, including the upcoming Latin American dates and the as-yet-unannounced European leg,” said the Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI) in a statement.

A pro-Palestinian rally is scheduled near the concert venue before the show on Saturday.

Artists in Gaza painted a mural of Macklemore in a Palestinian flag in the rubble of Gaza City to show their support. Despite a ceasefire agreement, Israel continues to kill Palestinians in frequent strikes across Gaza, where many remain displaced and live without access to basic services.

“Thank you for using your voice for Palestine,” it reads.

“We wanted to send a message to thank rapper Macklemore in this simple way,” Anne Redwan, who designed and painted the mural with fellow artist Qusai al-Helo, told the Reuters news agency.

“As an artist living under siege here in Gaza, we are waiting for support from anyone who can see (the) persecution we live under,” added the 26-year-old. “We can paint murals bigger than this to express our feelings.”

Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran’s tour after saying “free Palestine” during a show in New Jersey on September 5 . The influential pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft , whose company owns a stadium where Sheeran was scheduled to play, pushed for the rapper to be dropped in response.

But the effort backfired, underscoring the shifting dynamics around support for Palestine in the US, where support for Israel was once largely unquestioned and reliably bipartisan.

That has changed since Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza, setting off a remarkable swing in public opinion that has seen support for Israel shrink to its lowest levels on record. Support has dropped across the political spectrum, but especially among political progressives and voters in the Democratic Party.

Many politicians and influential figures have struggled to adjust to the shifting landscape around the issue. Macklemore’s expulsion prompted an outpouring of support from members of the public, Palestinian rights groups, and fellow artists.

Sheeran released a statement saying that he is “not complicit” and denying that he was responsible for the decision.
